q: In an ________ process, the volume is constant so that work done is zero. (2026)
e: In an isochoric process, the volume remains constant (ΔV = 0), so no thermodynamic work is done (W = PΔV = 0).

q: Which of the following fields is primarily concerned with the study of systems involving energy in the form of heat and work? (2025)
e: Thermodynamics is the branch of physics that deals with heat, work, and energy transformations in physical systems.

q: ________ is the ratio of the total emissive power of an object to that of the blackbody, at the same temperature and wavelength. (2026)
e: Emissivity is defined as the ratio of the total emissive power of a body to that of a blackbody at the same temperature and wavelength.

q: In fluid, heat is mainly transferred by ________. (2025)
e: Convection is the dominant mode of heat transfer in fluids due to the movement of fluid particles.

q: Isochoric process occurs at constant ________. (2025)
e: An isochoric process is defined as a process in which the volume of the system remains constant.

q: SI unit of thermal conductivity of the material is ________. (2026)
a: watt per metre kelvin (W m⁻¹ K⁻¹)
e: The SI unit for thermal conductivity is watt per metre kelvin (W m⁻¹ K⁻¹).

q: Thermal efficiency for a heat engine is the ratio of work output to ________ input. (2025)
e: Thermal efficiency is the ratio of useful work output to total heat energy input.

q: The internal energy of an ideal gas is ________ to the absolute temperature. (2025)
e: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature and is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

q: All real engines are ________ efficient than Carnot engine. (2025)
e: No real engine operating between two temperatures can be more efficient than a Carnot engine operating between the same limits.

q: An ________ process occurs at a constant temperature. (2025)
e: An isothermal process takes place at a constant temperature throughout.

q: Heat transfer processes are primarily studied in which field? (2025)
e: Thermodynamics covers heat transfer mechanisms along with thermal energy transformations.

q: What is the SI unit of thermal conductivity? (2025)
e: The SI unit of thermal conductivity is W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.

q: Which method of heat transfer does not require a medium? (2025)
e: Radiation transfers heat via electromagnetic waves and can travel through a vacuum without a material medium.

q: The total emissive power of objects other than a black body is ________. (2025)
e: The emissive power of a non-black body is proportional to its emissivity times the emissive power of a blackbody (ε = eε₀).

q: For a gas system, how many work is done in an isometric process? (2025)
e: In an isometric (isochoric) process, the volume does not change, so no work is done (W = 0).

q: Heat convection process takes place in a ________. (2025)
e: Convection requires particle motion, which occurs only in fluids (liquids and gases).

q: Which is a transfer of heat that does not require a material medium? (2021)
e: Heat radiation transfers energy by electromagnetic waves without needing a physical medium.

q: In which medium does the heat conduction take place? (2021)
e: Heat conduction primarily occurs in solids due to tightly packed molecular structures.

q: The ________ law of thermodynamics is an application of conservation energy for heat and thermodynamic processes. (2025)
e: The first law of thermodynamics is the application of the principle of conservation of energy to thermal systems.

q: An isobaric process occurs at constant ________. (2025)
e: An isobaric process is a thermodynamic process in which the pressure remains constant.

q: An isothermal process occurs at a constant ________. (2026)
e: An isothermal process occurs at constant temperature.

q: Heat conduction occurs most rapidly in ________. (2026)
e: Metals have high thermal conductivity due to free electrons that facilitate rapid heat transport.

q: An ideal gas undergoes an isothermal expansion. What can be said about the change in its internal energy (ΔU)? (2026)
e: For an ideal gas undergoing an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant, so ΔU = 0.
